programme.title: After Dark
programme.desc: After Dark was a British late night live discussion programme broadcast on Channel 4 television between 1987 and 1997, and on the BBC in 2003. Inspired by an Austrian programme called Club 2, Roly Keating of the BBC described it as "one of the great television talk formats of all time". In 2010 the television trade magazine Broadcast wrote "After Dark defined the first 10 years of Channel 4, just as Big Brother did for the second".

programme.title: Waka Huia
programme.desc: For over 100 years Mataatua wharepuni was uprooted from its home soil in Whakatāne, over 100 years in which Ngāti Awa could not be there to keep its fires burning. Ngāti Awa still mourns. Let the ancestral carvings of the house that came home arise! Arise! (R)

programme.title: Waka Huia
programme.desc: 100 years ago, land was stolen from the tribe of Ngati-Oneone in the East Coast of New Zealand. The land was taken from them to build a port, now known as, ‘Gisborne Port.’ After years of debating to give the land back and not being heard, the decedents of Rawiri Te Eketu o te Rangi have decided to march and take occupation over the land that is rightfully theirs. (R)

programme.title: Waka Huia
programme.desc: A proud son of Ngāti Manawa, war veteran Richard Dargaville, once a soldier for the New Zealand Army, he remains forever a soldier for te ao Māori. His service reflects not just commitment to a nation, but a deep dedication to whakapapa, identity, and the ongoing struggles and strengths of his whānau and wider Māori communities. (R)

programme.title: Waka Huia
programme.desc: Through the act of karanga, we traverse both the physical and spiritual realms, guided by ancestral voices that echo through time. This sacred practice is far more than a ritual—it is a powerful form of cultural expression that binds the living with those who have passed on. Within the context of Whiria te hono, a distinguished collective of kaikaranga from Ngāti Whātua Ōrākei, the spiritual and practical responsibilities of this tradition are deeply honoured and carefully upheld. These wāhine carry the weight of generations with each call, embodying the values, stories, and mana of their iwi. (R)

programme.title: Waka Huia
programme.desc: Charlie Rahiri describes himself as a reluctant iwi leader. But he was destined by his kaumātua to lead his iwi, Ngati Ranginui. He’s a direct descendant of Iwi chief Paraone Koikoi who surrendered his guns and pouches to the colonial office in 1864, only to be back in his kainga in Taumata three years later fighting for his land by pulling up survey pegs. We look at the changing role of a Māori Leader in Modern society through the eyes of Charlie Rahiri. (R)

programme.title: Waka Huia

programme.title: Waka Huia
programme.desc: The life and practice of Kumeroa Gregory, a skilled rongoā and weaving practitioner. Raised in Te Urewera under the guidance of her kuia and koroua, Ruakenana, Kumeroa’s journey took a significant turn in 1970 when she moved north. (R)

programme.title: Waka Huia
programme.desc: Te Taepa Kameta is one of the most prolific song writers and composers of this time. This episode of Waka Huia reveals where it all began while looking ahead to his future kapa haka ambitions. (R)

programme.title: Waka Huia
programme.desc: Te Reo a Tū explores how Te Arawa experts are reviving mau rākau. We hear from key voices on restoring this once-lost art and the vision to grow it in the community today. (R)

programme.title: Waka Huia
programme.desc: In the heart of Wairoa stands Tākitimu Marae — a place that has weathered the storms of Cyclones Bola and Gabrielle. Its people rise again. Through their hands and hearts, the marae and its taonga tuku iho are restored, breathing life back into the ancestral home that continues to shelter their stories. (R)

programme.title: Waka Huia
programme.desc: we cross the waters of Tauranga Moana to the island of Matakana. There, we meet the people of Oruarahi Marae and explore the rich histories of the land and their ancestor, Te Rangihouhiri. We journey back to a time when Oruarahi was thriving, tracing how the marae fell into disrepair, and hear the powerful story of its awakening and restoration — and what it took to bring the marae back to life. (R)

programme.title: Waka Huia
programme.desc: Māori entrepreneurs Piripi Winiata, Te Uranga Lee-Belk and Peter Lucas explain why it’s important for future generations to understand history behind the Māori economy and investment, in order to build sustainable wealth as part of a wider self-autonomy (mana motuhake) movement. programme.title: Waka Huia
programme.desc: For more 35 years, the people of Waimārama have fought to reclaim their reo and revive their marae, training speakers, running Kura Reo, and calling their whānau home. Now, with a new whare and their first Ahurei, that hard-won momentum is stronger than ever — a living invitation for descendants to return, reconnect, and help carry the kaupapa forward. (R)

programme.title: Waka Huia
programme.desc: 100 years ago, land was stolen from the tribe of Ngati-Oneone in the East Coast of New Zealand. The land was taken from them to build a port, now known as, ‘Gisborne Port.’ After years of debating to give the land back and not being heard, the decedents of Rawiri Te Eketu o te Rangi have decided to march and take occupation over the land that is rightfully theirs. (R)

programme.title: Waka Huia
programme.desc: A proud son of Ngāti Manawa, war veteran Richard Dargaville, once a soldier for the New Zealand Army, he remains forever a soldier for te ao Māori. His service reflects not just commitment to a nation, but a deep dedication to whakapapa, identity, and the ongoing struggles and strengths of his whānau and wider Māori communities. (R)

programme.title: Waka Huia
programme.desc: Through the act of karanga, we traverse both the physical and spiritual realms, guided by ancestral voices that echo through time. This sacred practice is far more than a ritual—it is a powerful form of cultural expression that binds the living with those who have passed on. Within the context of Whiria te hono, a distinguished collective of kaikaranga from Ngāti Whātua Ōrākei, the spiritual and practical responsibilities of this tradition are deeply honoured and carefully upheld. These wāhine carry the weight of generations with each call, embodying the values, stories, and mana of their iwi. (R)

programme.title: Waka Huia
programme.desc: Charlie Rahiri describes himself as a reluctant iwi leader. But he was destined by his kaumātua to lead his iwi, Ngati Ranginui. He’s a direct descendant of Iwi chief Paraone Koikoi who surrendered his guns and pouches to the colonial office in 1864, only to be back in his kainga in Taumata three years later fighting for his land by pulling up survey pegs. We look at the changing role of a Māori Leader in Modern society through the eyes of Charlie Rahiri. (R)

programme.title: Reel Rock
programme.desc: World class rock climber Leo Houlding, Cumbrian climber Anna Taylor and jungle expert Waldo Etherington undertake a big wall expedition to climb a new route on the overhanging prow of Mount Roraima.

programme.title: Reel Rock
programme.desc: With the first three pitches sent, the team’s “secret weapon”, Anna Taylor, must conquer the hardest pitch so far to keep the dream of a team free ascent alive.

programme.title: Reel Rock
programme.sub-title: The Hurt: Alex Honnold in Nevada Part 2
programme.desc: With nine routes down in the blazing sun and nine more to go, Alex Honnold gears up for the hardest climb so far – Nevada's Red Rock Canyon – just in time for nightfall.

programme.title: Veeco: A Volcom Filmmaking Documentary
programme.sub-title: Veeco unveiled – untold stories behind groundbreaking films
programme.desc: Take a journey through the Volcom film library and go behind the scenes with the filmmakers and riders as they share tales of blood, sweat and drama from Veeco Productions’ inception to the present.

programme.title: Pushing Progression
programme.desc: This is the story of freestyle football – and how the scene around it has transcended sport and established Red Bull Street Style as a competition that brings the world together.

programme.title: Red Bull Rapids 2022
programme.desc: This wild race sees teams create their own man-made vessels and race down a 234m whitewater rapids course where some will cross the finish line... while others may not.

programme.title: Pushing Progression
programme.desc: Explore the evolution of kiteboarding through the eyes of athletes like Robby Naish and see how events like Red Bull King of the Air and Red Bull Megaloop are pushing the progression of the sport.

programme.title: How Luke Czepiela Landed a Plane on a Tiny Helipad
programme.sub-title: The story behind Luke Czepiela’s iconic skyscraper plane landing
programme.desc: Luke Czepiela pushed the limits of aviation and landed a plane on the famous helipad of Burj Al Arab Jumeirah in Dubai. We take a closer look behind the scenes of the project with unique footage.

programme.title: Pushing Progression
programme.desc: Kyle Strait, Cam McCaul, Jaxson Riddle and Hannah Bergemann look at what’s fuelled innovation in freeride MTB. Purveyor of progression, skier Lindsey Vonn joins the cast as a special guest.

programme.title: Red Bull Signature Series
programme.desc: In this innovative evolution of Supercross a track is 'unwound' – no turns, just a half-mile-long straight rhythm section. The format pitted 32 riders in a head-to-head showdown of pure MX racing.

programme.title: Red Bull Signature Series
programme.desc: Thirteen of the world's best skateboarders compete at Ryan Sheckler’s private skate park for Red Bull Solus. Relive the most memorable moments from the inaugural edition.

programme.title: Red Bull Signature Series
programme.desc: A brand new event created by Tyler Bereman, Red Bull Imagination saw the world’s best freeriders tackle a unique course in order to showcase their slopestyle creativity.

programme.title: Red Bull Soapbox Race
programme.desc: What do flying Italian bagpipes and South Africa's fastest Stone Age racer have in common? They both made the cut among 2018's best Red Bull Soapbox Race runs.

programme.title: Red Bull Soapbox Race
programme.desc: With racing on four continents for the first time, 2019's races showcased some ultra-fast runs, but which teams won these wacky races?

programme.title: Unrideable
programme.desc: Wade Young aims to prove his worth as a privateer in the 2024 Xross Hard Enduro Rally and Red Bull Romaniacs after being dropped by his old team for Teodor Kabakchiev.

programme.title: Unrideable
programme.desc: Billy Bolt returns, as Mario Román chases his title dream. The rivals battle in Türkiye, racing literally from sea to sky.

programme.title: Unrideable
programme.desc: Big drama kicks off at 24MX Hixpania Hard Enduro – the 2024 season finale. Can Manuel Lettenbichler win the World Championship again or will someone else rise to glory?

programme.title: For Reals
programme.sub-title: From soapbox madness to skydiving with an FMX bike
programme.desc: Snowboarding – or, rather sandboarding – in the desert. Rally cars on frozen lakes. The wackiness of soapbox racing. Skydiving with a motocross bike. It's all in a day's work for Red Bull athletes!

programme.title: For Reals
programme.sub-title: From F1 soapbox racing to breaking world records
programme.desc: Breaking world records – it's all in a day's work for Red Bull athletes! See Felix Baumgartner jump from space, 65 women skydive together and one BMXer conquer the globe's biggest full loop.
